# Ajaia AI Trainer Assessment (Director Level)

## Objective

This assignment is designed to assess whether you can **credibly lead and deliver AI training in a real-world environment**.

We are evaluating your ability to:
- design a focused, practical AI training session  
- translate AI capabilities into real workflows and use cases  
- communicate clearly and confidently in a live training setting  
- demonstrate AI tools in action, not just describe them  
- engage an audience with structured, outcome-driven delivery  
- operate with strong judgment, clarity, and presence  

This is **not a theoretical training design exercise**.  

This is a **live delivery and demonstration assessment**.

---

## Time Limit

Please spend **no more than 3 hours total** on this assignment.

We are not evaluating polish or completeness.  

We are evaluating:
- clarity of thinking  
- practicality of training design  
- strength of communication and delivery  
- ability to demonstrate real AI usage  

---

## Scenario

You are leading an AI training session for a **healthcare organization (300–800 employees)**.

The audience may include:
- operations staff  
- administrative teams  
- managers  

Most participants:
- have limited experience with AI tools  
- are skeptical about usefulness  
- are concerned about workflow disruption  

Your goal is to design and deliver a **short training session that makes AI immediately useful and actionable**.

---

## Core Assignment

You are required to complete **three core outputs**:

---

## 1. Training Design (Concise)

Design a **short AI training program**.

### Include:

**Objective**
- What should participants be able to do after the session?

**Target Audience**
- Be specific (e.g., front desk staff, operations managers, etc.)

**Session Structure (30–45 minutes)**
- Key sections or flow of the session

**Core AI Workflow**
- Define at least **one practical workflow** you will teach  
- This must be something participants can realistically apply in their job  

**Examples:**
- automating patient communication responses  
- summarizing clinical or operational notes  
- drafting reports or follow-ups  
- scheduling or coordination support  

Your design should be **simple, focused, and outcome-driven**.

---

## 2. Presentation Deck

Create a **training presentation deck** that supports your session.

### The deck should:

- follow a clear training flow  
- be easy to understand for non-technical users  
- guide the audience toward action, not just information  
- support your live explanation (not replace it)  

### Include:

- problem framing (why this matters)  
- simple explanation of the AI capability  
- step-by-step workflow breakdown  
- prompts, examples, or inputs used  
- expected outputs or results  
- key takeaways or best practices  

Avoid overloading slides. Prioritize **clarity and usability**.

---

## 3. Live Training & Demo (Video)

Record yourself delivering a **short training segment (5–8 minutes total)**.

### Your video must include:

#### A. Training Delivery Segment
- explain part of your training clearly  
- walk through your slides  
- demonstrate structured teaching (not just reading slides)  

#### B. Live AI Demo
- show a real AI workflow in action  
- demonstrate inputs → process → outputs  
- explain what you are doing and why  
- show how this would be used in a real job context  

### We are evaluating:

- communication clarity  
- confidence and presence  
- ability to simplify concepts  
- ability to demonstrate, not just explain  
- practical usefulness of the workflow  

---

## Required: Candidate Video Introduction

In addition to the training video, please submit a **short video introduction (1–2 minutes)**.

### Include:
- your background  
- your experience with AI or training  
- why you are interested in this role  

Please upload this as an **unlisted YouTube video** (or equivalent) and include the link in your submission.

---

## Required: Prior Training Session Evidence (Separate Submission)

In addition to the training demo and introduction video, you are required to submit **evidence of a real training session you have previously delivered**.

This is a **separate requirement** from your introduction video.

### You must provide **at least one** of the following:

- A **recording of an actual training session** you conducted (full or partial), or  
- A **recorded segment of you facilitating a real class, workshop, or course**, or  
- A **client-facing training session recording**, or  
- If video is not available:  
  - **Training materials** (deck, curriculum, exercises) **AND**  
  - A **brief recorded walkthrough (2–5 minutes)** explaining how you delivered the session in a real setting  

### Important Notes:

- The session should reflect **real delivery experience**, not a recreated demo  
- The audience can be internal teams, clients, or external learners  
- The topic does **not have to be AI**, but AI-related training is preferred  
- Keep it concise. You may submit a **trimmed or partial recording** if needed  

---

## AI Workflow Note

Include a short note describing:
- which AI tools you used  
- how you used them  
- what they accelerated  
- what decisions and outputs were your own  

We expect candidates to use AI. We are evaluating **how effectively you use it**.

---

## Deliverables

Please submit the following:

- `1 training design (concise document or slides)`  
- `1 presentation deck`  
- `1 training + demo video (5–8 minutes)`  
- `1 candidate introduction video (1–2 minutes)`  
- `1 prior training session evidence (video or materials + walkthrough)`  
- `1 AI workflow note`  

---

## Submission Format

Submit **one Google Drive folder link** containing all materials.

In your application, include:
- your **Google Drive folder link**  
- your **training/demo video link**  
- your **introduction video link**  

---

## What We Will Evaluate

We will evaluate your submission based on:

- clarity and practicality of training design  
- relevance and usefulness of the AI workflow  
- strength of live demonstration  
- communication clarity and structure  
- confidence and presence during delivery  
- ability to simplify complex ideas  
- alignment with real-world workflows  
- effective use of AI tools  
- demonstrated real-world training experience and delivery capability  

---

## Constraints

- Maximum time: **3 hours**  
- Keep it focused and practical  
- Do not overproduce slides or content  
- Prioritize **demonstration over explanation**  
- Prioritize **clarity over completeness**  

---

## Key Principle

Strong candidates will:
- **show, not just tell**  
- teach something immediately useful  
- demonstrate real AI usage clearly  
- communicate with confidence and structure  

Weak candidates will:
- stay too theoretical  
- avoid live demonstration  
- over-focus on slides instead of delivery  
- fail to connect AI to real work
